rv.q: I had never seen the play before and last night it knocked me for six with its emotional truth and extraordinarily powerful depiction of the devastation caused by alcoholism.
But Odets wrote a gift part for a star actor, and it is one that Shaw seizes avidly by conveying the fear that lurks beneath the smell of the greasepaint.
This is a wonderful play, about acting and the theatre, deception and love, and it deserves to hit home harder and to be “voiced” more gorgeously.
But there is much sting and sharp edges in The Country Girl.

cn.t: Odets' backstage drama about an alcoholic actor earns praise for its emotional power and sharp direction, though some find it slow-burning and slightly miscast. A lively, well-designed revival that divides critics.
